sections.title: Intake
sections.conclusion: Baseline fields and source anchors establish whether the proposal can be reviewed at all.

sections.title: Claims and evidence
findings: Proposal document read by reasoning layer: yes
Requested: Build an open, Cardano-anchored trust layer for global agricultural supply chains using Veridian self-sovereign identity and a Cardano on-chain satellite oracle
Deliverables: M1 Stand-Up (Month 6), M2 Closed Loop (Month 12), M3 Self-Sustaining (Month 18), 500,000 registered farmers across India, Cambodia and Kenya
Claim (adoption, proposer_asserted, high materiality): The programme will reach 500,000 registered farmers across India, Cambodia and Kenya during the funded period
Claim (economic, independently_verifiable, medium materiality): Around 500 million smallholder farmers lack formal trust infrastructure that lenders, insurers and certifiers rely on
Claim (technical, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The 18-month programme is structured around three named milestones (M1 Stand-Up, M2 Closed Loop, M3 Self-Sustaining)
Claim (technical, proposer_asserted, high materiality): The trust layer combines Veridian self-sovereign identity with a Cardano on-chain satellite oracle and will become self-sustaining
missing: Independent evidence for: The programme will reach 500,000 registered farmers across India, Cambodia and Kenya during the funded period
Independent evidence for: The trust layer combines Veridian self-sovereign identity with a Cardano on-chain satellite oracle and will become self-sustaining
sections.conclusion: Each claim must map to replayable public evidence; proposer assertions alone are not enough for confidence.

sections.title: Treasury analysis
sections.conclusion: Treasury votes require a higher bar because they consume shared ADA and create precedent.

sections.title: Risk review
sections.conclusion: Risk is not a side note; unmitigated execution or governance risk can dominate an otherwise attractive proposal.

sections.title: Counterargument pass
findings: Strongest YES: the proposal substantiates "Around 500 million smallholder farmers lack formal trust infrastructure that lenders, insurers and certifiers rely on" and clears the evidence gates.

Strongest NO: a material claim is unsupported — "The programme will reach 500,000 registered farmers across India, Cambodia and Kenya during the funded period" — so cost or precedent may outweigh the benefit.
Strongest hold: a treasury action without a complete deep-research dossier cannot be voted directionally without pretending certainty.
sections.conclusion: A defensible rationale must show the best opposing case before it reaches a vote.

sections.title: Synthesis
findings: Final vote must be derived from completed sections above, not from a prose summary.
The public rationale should name the decisive section and the strongest counterargument.
sections.conclusion: The vote is only credible if the assessment tree shows enough work for a skeptical delegator to audit.
